Stop work / unsafe conditions — needs confirmation, not action

These are selections on the air job OWL forms, not confirmed events. Technicians sometimes select "Unsafe conditions" because they regard wellhead work as inherently unsafe rather than because a specific condition arose. Note first that "Stop work authority utilized" was not selected on a single form today. Where stop-work appears at all it is "Stop work authority was discussed", which is a routine pre-job item.
"Unsafe conditions" was selected on two forms:

Raymundo Solis, XTO Preston-Freeman 15I 109H, job 37116, 12:40 PM — selected alongside "Stop work authority was discussed". The narrative is positive, not adverse: "The use of tag line - the crew member that was in charge of the tag line held it with proper technique and made sure it wasn't wrapped around his hand". No narrative on the form describes an actual unsafe condition. This looks like the mis-selection pattern and needs his confirmation.

1099 Kedrick McCarter, XTO University 58-17B 2H, job 37171, 2:20 PM — selected alongside "Stop work authority was discussed". Here the narrative does name a condition: "A leak well and had to change the nipple".

One item is not the mis-selection pattern and should be read the other way round. 1099 Hayden Haugh worked the same job, University 58-17B 2H, job 37170, and his narrative records the same leak — "Crew changed out a nipple on the 90 due to it leaking" and "Nipple change out on the 90" — but he did not select "Unsafe conditions". Two technicians on one job reported the same leaking wellhead component and only one flagged it. That is the inverse problem to the usual one and is worth raising as a training point alongside the over-selection.
Michael Jobe appeared on this list on 09/26/2026 for selecting "Unsafe conditions" with no supporting narrative; he was clear on 11/11 and is clear again today.

Two forms carried an entirely empty "What did we observe?" multi-select, which is the opposite failure — nothing selected at all: 1099 Gage Gonzales on job 37152 (Preston-Shackelford 15K 11H) and 1099 Bobby Galindo on job 36448.

Trailer forms of both kinds, and the equipment sections of the H2S daily, are photo-based. A defect visible only in a photograph would not surface in this review. Fire extinguisher inspection and expiration dates, first aid kit dates and 4-gas calibration dates exist only inside the images, not as text fields, so this review can confirm that a photo was taken and when it was taken, but not what it shows.

88 of 88 submissions read. The job board was available: Blake Walton's 11/19/2026 Ark-La-Tex & Permian Basin boards arrived at 10:01 AM and the 11-19 sheet of each was used. 42 manned Permian rows and 12 manned ETX rows were checked for coverage. This run started at 11:06 PM Central, before the Central day closed, so forms submitted after that time are not in these counts — missing Trailer Readiness Forms and second Trailer Inspection Forms are the findings most often resolved by a late submission, and no next-morning search was possible because the following morning has not yet happened. One further form arrived in the window but carries a form date of 11/18/2026 — a Trailer Readiness Form for trailer 501 submitted by 1099 Trevor McKenzie at 1:58 PM on 11/18. It was read but belongs to that day and is not counted toward today's coverage.
